description: A two-panel composite figure reporting instrumented Charpy impact testing of an experimental Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel at -196 °C, -77 °C and room temperature (RT). Panel (a) shows load-deflection curves: Charpy impact load (kN, y-axis 0-35) versus Deflection (mm, x-axis 0-25), with three filled profiles colour-keyed by the legend -196 °C (pink), -77 °C (blue) and RT (grey). The -196 °C curve reaches the highest peak, just above the 30 kN line, and falls steeply to zero before ~8 mm deflection; the -77 °C curve peaks lower and drops near ~11 mm; the grey RT curve has the lowest peak (within the 20-25 kN band) and extends furthest, beyond 20 mm. Panel (b) is a stacked bar chart of Impact absorbed energy (J, y-axis 0-350) versus Temperature (°C) at -196, -77 and 25, each bar divided into W_initiation (bottom, cream), W_stable (middle, orange) and W_unstable (top, dark olive) segments; bar totals are printed as 188 J, 277 J and 327 J. Together the panels show that decreasing test temperature raises peak load but shortens deflection to fracture and lowers total absorbed energy, while the relative initiation and unstable-crack contributions grow at cryogenic temperature.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots Charpy impact load (kN) on a 0-35 kN axis against Deflection (mm) on a 0-25 mm axis, with a legend giving -196 °C (pink), -77 °C (blue) and RT (grey) load-deflection profiles.
In panel (a) the -196 °C curve attains the highest peak load, rising just above the 30 kN gridline, and returns to zero before about 8 mm deflection.
In panel (a) the RT (grey) curve has the lowest peak load, lying within the 20-25 kN band, and its load persists to the longest deflection, beyond 20 mm and extending past 25 mm.
Panel (a) shows an inverse relationship: as test temperature decreases from RT to -77 °C to -196 °C, peak impact load increases while the deflection at which load falls to zero decreases.
Panel (b) is a stacked bar chart with y-axis 'Impact absorbed energy (J)' from 0 to 350 and x-axis 'Temperature (°C)' with bars at -196, -77 and 25.
The legend of panel (b) defines three energy components: W_unstable (dark olive, top segment), W_stable (orange, middle segment) and W_initiation (cream, bottom segment).
Total absorbed energies printed above the bars of panel (b) are 188 J at -196 °C, 277 J at -77 °C and 327 J at 25 (RT).
The W_initiation segment occupies the largest fraction of the total bar at -196 °C and a progressively smaller fraction at -77 °C and 25, whereas W_stable becomes the dominant segment at RT.
The caption identifies (a) as the Charpy impact load and (b) as the Charpy impact absorbed energy of the experimental steel.
The citing text states that the W_all at RT is about 327 J and decreases to 277 J at -77 °C and 188 J at -196 °C.
The citing text attributes the lower W_all at cryogenic temperature to the increased activation energy for slip systems, which makes planar slip harder to activate and causes early fracture.
The citing text equates the total absorbed energy W_all with the quantity plotted as bar totals in panel (b); the panels themselves do not print the symbol 'W_all'.

subfigures.description: Load-deflection curves from instrumented Charpy impact tests: Charpy impact load (kN, 0-35) versus Deflection (mm, 0-25), three filled curves labelled -196 °C (pink), -77 °C (blue) and RT (grey). Peak load rises and deflection at fracture shortens as temperature decreases; the -196 °C curve peaks just above 30 kN and ends before ~8 mm, the -77 °C curve near ~11 mm, and the RT curve extends past 20 mm at the lowest peak load.

Stacked bar chart of Impact absorbed energy (J, 0-350) versus Temperature (°C) for -196, -77 and 25, with each bar split into W_initiation (bottom, cream), W_stable (middle, orange) and W_unstable (top, dark olive). Bar totals are printed as 188 J (-196), 277 J (-77) and 327 J (25); individual segment values are not labelled.
